tldr_label: TL;DR: Ukraine hits the Crimean Bridge, Russia hits Kyiv's bridges, Trump lands in Manila, and Wall Street slides before Nvidia reports

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Russian defense data show Ukraine launched the largest overnight drone attack of the war and hit the Crimean Bridge. Russian strikes then hit two Kyiv bridges, cutting water and power. [[TAG:danger:infrastructure war]]

tldr_bullets.label: Trump in Asia
tldr_bullets.body: Trump arrived in Manila for a US-ASEAN summit before going to Shenzhen. He says he may meet Kim Jong Un, but experts see no signs of preparation. [[TAG:info:summit week]]

tldr_bullets.label: Gulf
tldr_bullets.body: UKMTO confirmed a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile leaving Hormuz, while Iran claims more ships struck mines. Vance ruled out a 'forever war.' [[TAG:danger:shipping attacks]]

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The Nasdaq fell 2.5% on Monday after Commerce tightened rules on overseas Chinese access to AI chips. Nvidia reports after Tuesday's close. [[TAG:warning:earnings tonight]]

tldr_bullets.label: Europe
tldr_bullets.body: Five EU countries announced plans for a return hub in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers. Germany pressed Israel to let more aid into Gaza. [[TAG:info:migration shift]]

sections.title: Ukraine: The Bridge War
sections.summary: Record Ukrainian drone wave hits Crimean Bridge and refineries; Russia strikes Kyiv's bridges

paragraphs.heading: Record Drone Strike
paragraphs.body: NBC News and The Moscow Times reported that Ukraine launched what Russian defense data showed was the largest overnight drone attack of the war. Russia said it intercepted 1,336 drones. Bloomberg reported that the attack hit the Crimean Bridge, halting traffic. The Kremlin called the damage minor, while unverified images suggested a larger collapse. Ukraine's General Staff said it also struck the Ilsky refinery in Krasnodar region. [[TAG:danger:record attack]]

paragraphs.heading: Kyiv's Bridges
paragraphs.body: France 24 and Business Recorder reported that Russian strikes hit Kyiv's North and South bridges over the Dnipro, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko, cutting water and power in parts of the city. The Cyprus Mail reported that Russia's defense ministry said it hit transport, military and energy targets in several regions. Zelensky said intelligence pointed to more Russian strikes into Tuesday. [[TAG:danger:water and power cut]]

sections.title: Trump in Asia
sections.summary: Trump lands in Manila for US-ASEAN and Quad talks; floats a Kim meeting experts doubt

paragraphs.heading: Manila
paragraphs.body: The Manila Times and Rappler reported that Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday, his first visit to the Philippines in nine years, for a US-ASEAN special summit, a Quad leaders' meeting and talks with President Marcos. He skipped the East Asia Summit. Rappler reported that hundreds of people have been arrested in protests since the ASEAN summit opened. [[TAG:info:Shenzhen next]]

paragraphs.heading: Kim Floated
paragraphs.body: Bloomberg and ABC News reported that Trump said he may meet North Korea's Kim Jong Un in China, adding that it was 'up to President Xi.' The Korea Times reported that experts see no signs of working-level preparation, and North Korea is not an APEC member. The trilateral with Xi and Putin remains set for Thursday. [[TAG:warning:no preparation seen]]

sections.title: Gulf: Tankers Under Fire
sections.summary: UKMTO confirms a tanker hit leaving Hormuz; Bahrain blames Iran; Vance rules out 'forever war'

paragraphs.heading: Shipping
paragraphs.body: SANA and JNS reported that UKMTO said a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while exiting the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, causing an engine-room fire, with no casualties reported. Seatrade Maritime reported two tankers confirmed struck, while Iran claims a VLCC sank. Iran's navy says more ships have hit mines. The cause of the incidents, whether mines, missiles or both, is unresolved, and dates differ across reports. [[TAG:danger:confirmed strike]]

paragraphs.heading: Bahrain
paragraphs.body: CBS News and The National reported that Bahrain's foreign ministry holds Iran 'fully responsible' for drone attacks on Friday and Sunday, all of which were intercepted. The National reported that Gulf markets fell, with Qatar's index down 1.8%. [[TAG:warning:Gulf markets fall]]

paragraphs.heading: Vance
paragraphs.body: TRT World and Newsweek reported that Vice President Vance told Fox News the administration will not let the Iran war become a 'forever war' and ruled out a 10- or 15-year commitment, while denying any rift with Trump. He acknowledged the war and higher energy prices hurt Republicans in the midterms but gave no timetable. [[TAG:info:no timetable]]

sections.title: Markets: Chips Under Pressure
sections.summary: Nasdaq drops 2.5% as Commerce closes an AI chip loophole; Kospi falls below 5,000

paragraphs.heading: Wall Street
paragraphs.body: CNN and STL.News, citing Reuters, reported that the Dow fell 1.41%, the S&P 500 1.92% and the Nasdaq 2.49% on Monday. Nvidia closed down 4.12% at $156.14, its lowest close since July 2025, and CNN said it is down roughly 35% from its October record. Nvidia reports after Tuesday's close. [[TAG:danger:Nasdaq -2.5%]]

paragraphs.heading: Commerce Rule
paragraphs.body: CNBC and Fortune reported that the Commerce Department issued an interim final rule closing a loophole that let Chinese firms use Nvidia chips in third-country data centers. The rule extends controls to Southeast Asian countries including Singapore and Malaysia. It follows criticism, reported by Axios, that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had stalled chip controls. CNBC also reported that Nvidia warned customers of legal risks tied to Chinese access to chip capacity. [[TAG:warning:tighter controls]]

paragraphs.heading: Asia
paragraphs.body: AP, via US News, reported that South Korea's Kospi fell 2.6% on Tuesday to close below 5,000 for the first time since February. Reports put the Nikkei down about 1.2% to 1.3%, led by AI-linked stocks. FXStreet said the US tech curbs weighed on sentiment. [[TAG:warning:AI selloff]]

sections.title: Europe and Asia Security
sections.summary: Russian planes breach Japanese airspace; five EU states plan a Rwanda return hub

paragraphs.heading: Airspace
paragraphs.body: The Japan Times reported that Japan scrambled fighters after two suspected Russian military planes entered its airspace off Fukuoka, and Tokyo lodged a protest. South Korea also scrambled jets when Russian aircraft entered its air defense identification zone, though Seoul said its airspace was not violated. It was Japan's first confirmed Russian airspace violation since 2024. [[TAG:warning:airspace breach]]

paragraphs.heading: Rwanda Hub
paragraphs.body: SCMP and KSL reported that five European countries announced plans to send rejected asylum seekers to a return hub in Rwanda, aiming to open it by 2027 under the EU's new Return Regulation. No agreement has been signed. Rights groups oppose the plan, and UNHCR said it is in 'constructive discussions' with the countries. [[TAG:info:2027 target]]

sections.title: Israel and Gaza
sections.summary: No progress in Likud talks as Eisenkot courts UTJ; Germany presses Israel on Gaza aid

paragraphs.heading: Coalition
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel reported no progress in the Yashar-Likud unity talks and said Netanyahu is open to excluding Ben Gvir. The Jerusalem Post reported that Eisenkot is pushing to bring United Torah Judaism into government while Netanyahu tries to block a deal. The Haredi demand for a draft arrangement before any swearing-in is seen as the hardest obstacle. The Times of Israel said the Knesset faces a pivotal week as Eisenkot's bloc seeks to replace the speaker. [[TAG:warning:draft obstacle]]

paragraphs.heading: Aid
paragraphs.body: Middle East Monitor reported that German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul urged Israel to let more aid into Gaza before winter. Yahoo News reported that Wadephul said Israel will start using German-supplied cargo scanners to speed aid checks, after he called the delay unacceptable. [[TAG:info:scanners approved]]

sections.title: Pope Heads Home
sections.summary: Leo leaves Peru after an intensive South America tour, due back in Rome on Tuesday

paragraphs.heading: Farewell
paragraphs.body: Vatican News and EWTN reported that Pope Leo XIV left Lima on Monday, ending a South American tour that began November 6 and covered Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. He was due to land in Rome on Tuesday. Yahoo News reported that he told reporters on the flight he felt fine and joked that they looked more tired than him. [[TAG:success:tour complete]]
